text:
Matvei Michkov is the story in Philadelphia, and not for his 10 goals. On Tuesday ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported that Michkov would welcome a fresh start elsewhere; GM Danny Briere answered that neither Michkov nor his agent asked for a trade and the Flyers have no plan to move him. Daily Faceoff ran a piece on Michkov's ego and the drama. Whatever is true behind closed doors, a season 21 games old now has a subplot that won't go away quietly.

On the ice, the Flyers are 5-10-6 and the chances explain most of it. They have 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 43% at five on five, and allow 3.37 expected goals an hour. Their shooters have scored almost 10 fewer goals than their chances deserved, so the record is a little worse than the play, but the play hasn't been good. The last ten games, at 49% of the chances, have been closer to even.

There are pieces worth watching. Michkov's line with Noah Cates and Porter Martone has 61% of the chances in about 105 minutes together. Travis Sanheim and Jamie Drysdale have been the best pair, 10-6. Travis Konecny and Owen Tippett are back from injuries, and Rasmus Ristolainen returned on Wednesday, picking up an assist in a 3-2 overtime loss in Edmonton that the Flyers deserved to win.

Our numbers give Philadelphia a 3% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 76 points.
